# P2a independent performance review: current source

**PASS for static source review.** No blocking source-backed performance finding.
The reviewed source is `6fb7f94173320326bd523a8af67db77916ac7da3` in
`/workspace/android-studio-import-identity-getters`. This verdict does not satisfy
runtime performance, full-app, native, all-feature, Clippy or lead merge gates.

## Work performed

Read the repository `.rules`, the additive Gradle bridge, the full Rust decoder,
its 30 supplemental tests, the task report, and the existing Basic-model sync,
stdout capture and cancellation code. Compared the bridge to base
`0d72037ca895893e8cf338d5ade8b37b1bb645b8`. Independently verified every one of
4,738 current source paths and hashes against the fixed seven-pattern snapshot,
and all six retained API/helper references against their attributed manifest.
No Cargo, rustc, Clippy, JVM, Gradle, SDK, native or application command was run.
No source, runtime, cache or repository metadata was changed.

## Static checks

1. **Gradle work stays within the existing sync invocation.** The production
   diff adds a graph-ready callback and serialization fields. It adds no task,
   task dependency, build action or Gradle invocation. The callback runs after
   project-evaluation listeners and traverses the root catalogue once. It calls
   ten identity getters per catalogue entry and repeats the ten getters for the
   root build observation. Those counts describe source operations, not elapsed
   time. The getter bodies do not apply plugins, touch configurations, resolve
   dependencies or realize Providers. Existing Basic/V2 producer tasks and their
   owner-project collection are unchanged. The supplemental `kodaIdentityOracle`
   task belongs to a private authored fixture, not the production bridge.

2. **Catalogue validation avoids a quadratic project scan.** The raw vector
   retains captured order. One `BTreeMap<String, usize>` indexes local paths;
   insertion detects duplicates, parent checks and Basic-module matching use the
   index, and public project lookup borrows the indexed entry. With P catalogue
   projects and M Basic modules, these stages require O(P log P + M log P)
   comparisons, plus validation of field bytes. String comparison costs depend
   on path length. The map does not clone each entire project or reorder the
   observed catalogue. Tests cover reversed order, duplicates, missing parent
   holders, missing root and missing Basic-module identities.

3. **Decoding has an explicit accepted-record bound.** The Rust decoder rejects
   a record above 16 MiB before JSON allocation, and rejects a second model
   record. The supplemental boundary test accepts exactly 16 MiB and rejects one
   more byte. Output scanning is linear in supplied stdout bytes. Conversion of
   the sidecar and explicit result objects performs bounded additional work on
   that input. This is a wire-size acceptance bound, not a claim that peak heap
   is 16 MiB: JSON values, typed strings, path keys and identities also allocate.
   Production command capture already bounds total stdout at 16 MiB and preserves
   its existing log backpressure and process cancellation behavior.

4. **Freshness has a known, finite cost.** Decoding clones the Basic
   module/directory/kind/variant identity once. `ensure_current` compares revisions
   and selections first and, when those match, reconstructs and compares that
   identity. The latter allocates proportionally to Basic identity bytes on each
   call. Selection validation builds a Basic-module tree map and selected-variant
   tree set; variant membership scans only the selected module's variants.
   Its cost includes O(M log M + S log S + S log M), plus the sum of those
   variant scans for S selections. It is not a blanket O(P log P) claim for all
   decoding. The new snapshot is not yet wired into a render loop or foreground
   UI caller, so no present source establishes per-frame rebuilding or repeated
   UI blocking. Publication work should use freshness checks at operation/model
   boundaries and measure their cost before introducing frequent UI callers.

5. **Failure isolation preserves existing behavior.** Getter exceptions and
   linkage failures become unavailable observations without falling back to
   imports, retries, dependency resolution or a second Gradle process. Sidecar
   decoding returns typed errors separately from the caller's Basic model.
   Production Basic parsing, background sync execution and cancellation have not
   been changed by this task. This is source compatibility evidence; actual SDK,
   late-configuration and cancellation runs remain pending.

## Runtime follow-up; no performance measurements claimed

Canonical directory getters perform filesystem work; root paths are observed
again per project, and repeated getter provenance increases serialized bytes.
These are linear source costs with filesystem-dependent timing. JVM map/JSON
construction occurs before the Rust size rejection, so the accepted-record bound
is not a producer heap bound. The additive sidecar consumes part of the existing
16 MiB total stdout budget; real captures should record bytes and verify headroom
along with the existing Basic/V2 model. A representative large-project run is
still needed to measure capture duration, peak memory and cancellation
responsiveness. No startup, RSS, hardware rendering, benchmark improvement or
large-project runtime pass is asserted here.

The current owner receipt reports 30 default-feature tests passed, zero failed,
ignored or filtered, plus a default library build and workspace formatting pass.
I read that evidence and did not rerun it. It supplies no application or Gradle
performance measurement. All-feature tooling/build, strict repository Clippy,
actual Gradle/SDK oracle probes, full app/native workflow and lead CI remain
pending. Original naming/facet/Kotlin/tree tests receive zero new parity credit.

All previous reviews and failure evidence are preserved. Exact reviewed file
hashes, evidence hashes and source/index preservation checks are in the companion
JSON report.
